arxiv-2209-04806.title: Deep Learning Based DOA Estimation for Hybrid Massive MIMO Receive Array with Overlapped Subarrays
arxiv-2209-04806.creator: Yifan Li, Baihua Shi, Feng Shu, Member, IEEE, Yaoliang Song, Senior Member, IEEE, Jiangzhou Wang, Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2209-04806.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yifan Li, Baihua Shi, Feng Shu, Member, IEEE, Yaoliang Song, Senior Member, IEEE, Jiangzhou Wang, Fellow, IEEE. To improve the accuracy of direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation, a deep learning (DL)-based method called CDAE-DNN is proposed for hybrid analog and digital (HAD) massive MIMO receive array with overlapped subarray (OSA) architecture in this paper.

arxiv-2407-18230.title: Computation and stability analysis of periodic orbits using finite differences, Fourier or Chebyshev spectral expansions in time
arxiv-2407-18230.creator: Artur Gesla, Yohann Duguet, Patrick Le Quéré, Laurent Martin Witkowski
arxiv-2407-18230.description: Abstract We analyse and compare several algorithms to compute numerically periodic solutions of high-dimensional dynamical systems and investigate their Floquet stability without building the monodromy matrix. The solution and its perturbation are discretised in time either using finite differences, Fourier-Galerkin or Chebyshev expansions. The resulting nonlinear set of equations describing the periodic orbit is solved using a Newton-Raphson algorithm.

arxiv-2409-06095.description: Abstract . In this note we discuss the SBV \mathrm{SBV} -regularity for a scalar balance law in one space dimension as a case study in order to explain the strategy that we apply in [ 3 ] to systems of balance laws, generalizing [ 5 ] , [ 7 ] .

arxiv-2503-23750.title: Float Lattice Gas Automata: A connection between Molecular Dynamics and Lattice Boltzmann Method for quantum computers
arxiv-2503-23750.creator: Antonio David Bastida Zamora, Ljubomir Budinski, Pierre Sagaut, Valtteri Lahtinen
arxiv-2503-23750.description: Abstract Building upon the Integer Lattice Gas Automata framework of Blommel et al. Blommel and Wagner 2018 , we introduce a simplified, fluctuation-free variant. This approach relies on floating-point numbers and closely mirrors the Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM), with the key distinction being a novel collision operator. This operator, derived from the ensemble average of transition probabilities, generates nonlinear terms.

arxiv-2506-23016.title: Deep Learning in Mild Cognitive Impairment Diagnosis using Eye Movements and Image Content in Visual Memory Tasks
arxiv-2506-23016.creator: Tomás Silva Santos Rocha a, Anastasiia Mikhailova b, Moreno I. Coco c, José Santos-Victor d
arxiv-2506-23016.description: Abstract The global prevalence of dementia is projected to double by 2050, highlighting the urgent need for scalable diagnostic tools. This study utilizes digital cognitive tasks with eye-tracking data correlated with memory processes to distinguish between Healthy Controls (HC) and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), a precursor to dementia.

arxiv-2510-01237.title: Confidence-Aware Routing for Large Language Model Reliability Enhancement: A Multi-Signal Approach to Pre-Generation Hallucination Mitigation
arxiv-2510-01237.creator: Nandakishor M
arxiv-2510-01237.description: Abstract Large Language Models suffer from hallucination, generating plausible yet factually incorrect content. Current mitigation strategies focus on post-generation correction, which is computationally expensive and fails to prevent unreliable content generation. We propose a confidence-aware routing system that proactively assesses model uncertainty before generation and redirects queries based on estimated reliability.

arxiv-2512-18659.title: Measuring the Impact of Student Gaming Behaviors on Learner Modeling
arxiv-2512-18659.creator: Qinyi Liu, Lin Li, Valdemar Švábenský, Conrad Borchers, Mohammad Khalil
arxiv-2512-18659.description: Abstract . The expansion of large-scale online education platforms has yielded vast amounts of student interaction data for knowledge tracing (KT). KT models estimate students’ concept mastery from interaction data, but the models’ performance is sensitive to input data quality. Gaming behaviors, such as excessive hint use, may misrepresent students’ knowledge and undermine model reliability.

pmc-11276960.title: CTC-177, a novel drug–Fc conjugate, shows promise as an immunoprophylactic agent against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial infections
pmc-11276960.creator: Arianne Lovey, Annie Lee, Allison Yu, Mila Krel, Mingming Wang, Padmaja Paderu, Thomas Brady, Grayson Hough, Qiping Zhao, James M Balkovec, David S Perlin, Yanan Zhao

pmc-11618317.title: Hepatitis B clinical care provision in pregnancy: A whole‐of‐population linkage study in Victoria, Australia
pmc-11618317.creator: Jennifer H MacLachlan, Nicole Romero, Nicole Allard, Stacey L Rowe, Benjamin C Cowie
pmc-11618317.description: Background and AimPregnancy is a key setting for engagement in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) care, due to the implications for transmission to the infant and antenatal diagnosis representing an opportunity for ongoing follow‐up. This study aimed to identify the coverage and predictors of clinical care for women with CHB during and after pregnancy in a population‐level cohort.

pmc-12648481.title: Development of an in-house, one-step RT-qPCR mix and optimized MS2 detection primers for hepatitis A virus and norovirus detection in berries1
pmc-12648481.creator: Hui Zhi Low, Christina Böhnlein, Charles M.A.P. Franz
pmc-12648481.description: One-step, reverse transcriptase-quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) is the primary method for detecting foodborne viruses in food matrices. Some food matrices, such as berries, tend to co-purify PCR inhibitors with viral RNA, which can lead to false-negative results.

pmc-13700256.title: Radiographic outcomes and prognostic factors after protocol-defined prolonged abduction containment for Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease: a 427-hip retrospective cohort study
pmc-13700256.creator: Tiantian Xia, Fengjie Zhang, Jiaru Liao, Xiaoqiang Yang, Fan Yang, Wei He, Ziqi Li
pmc-13700256.description: BackgroundEvidence on nonoperative treatment for Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease remains limited by heterogeneity in treatment exposure, including variable combinations of observation, physiotherapy, bracing, casting, activity restriction, and weight-bearing restriction. We evaluated radiographic outcomes and risk factors after a protocol-defined prolonged cast-based abduction containment regimen, thereby establishing benchmark outcome estimates for this specific nonoperative pathway.
